title: No public envelope says which retrieval backend served the request
description:
No public `--json` envelope, on any command, exposes which retrieval backend actually served the request. `RetrievalGraph.backend` ("indexed" | "reference") exists internally and reaches nothing: `graph`, `query`, `context`, `path` and `impact` all drop it, and the only trace a fallback leaves is one line of stderr prose, present only when a fallback happened and absent when the indexed path ran.

So there is no POSITIVE signal at all. A consumer cannot prove the indexed backend ran, cannot prove it did not, and cannot assert on either.

WHY THIS IS ITS OWN TASK RATHER THAN A NOTE ON LCLI-497. 497 was a corruption that disabled the indexed backend on any tracker with a prerequisite. It was found by accident, and it could only have been found by accident, because nothing a caller can read says which backend answered. Fixing the corruption does not fix that; the next such defect is just as invisible as this one was.

Reported by opum-cli-e2e (session 75d492) 2026-09-14, after reading retrieval.ts, workspace-retrieval.ts and all five command files on origin/dev and confirming empirically against installed lore 0.6.2. They have added a row in suites/60-project-lifecycle.mjs (their TASK-63) that asserts the ABSENCE directly: it passes today and starts failing usefully the day such a field exists.

ONE PART OF THEIR REPORT IS NOT ACCURATE and is recorded here so it is not re-derived. They concluded that `graph`/`query`/`context` call `loadRetrievalGraph` only under `--workspace`, and that `path`/`impact` are therefore the only commands exercising the indexed pipeline in plain mode. That is true of `runGraph`'s own internal default and false of the CLI: src/cli.ts injects `retrieval: context.retrieval ?? loadRetrievalGraph` at five call sites covering all five commands, so a plain single-repo `lore graph` does go through the indexed pipeline. Measured directly -- `lore graph --plain` against this repository with LCLI-497 in place prints "native indexed retrieval failed; using the in-memory reference backend", which it could not do if it never called the loader.

The correction does not weaken their finding; it strengthens it. All five commands were affected by LCLI-497, not two, and still none of them can say so.

SHAPE TO DESIGN, not settled here: a `backend` field on the retrieval-family envelopes, present ALWAYS rather than only on fallback -- a marker that appears only in the degraded case cannot announce its own applicability, which is the same rule ADR-0021 applies to relation version state and LCLI-478 applies to omission reporting. Pairs with LCLI-498: this says WHICH backend, that one says WHY the other was not used.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The --json envelope of graph, query, context, path and impact names the backend that served the request
The field is present on every successful response, not only when a fallback occurred
A test asserts the field for both an indexed and a reference-backed run of the same command
opum-cli-e2e is told the field name and shape so their absence-assertion row can be flipped to a presence assertion

implementationNotes:
SCOPE ADDITION AND A SECOND FINDING, both 2026-09-14, both from opum-cli-e2e via opum-agent.

RULED INTO 0.7.0 by opum-agent alongside LCLI-497, with the reasoning recorded so it is not read as drift: 497 repairs the indexed backend, and this task is what makes it possible to know the repair holds. Shipping the fix without the detector fixes one instance and leaves the class undetectable, which is how LCLI-497 reached us -- found by accident three hours later, because nothing reported which path ran. It does not block the tag on its own, but it should land before opum-cli-e2e qualifies the pair, since their backend-identity row can otherwise only key on the ABSENCE of a stderr advisory.

THE SECOND FINDING MAKES THAT INFERENCE WORSE THAN "WEAK". There is a THIRD route to the reference backend under `policy: "auto"` that calls `warnReferenceFallback` not at all:

    if (lifecycle.generation === undefined) { if (policy === "indexed") throw indexedUnavailable(); return loadReferenceGraph(options); }

No indexed generation has been built for this bundle yet, so it returns the reference graph with no advisory whatsoever. Empty stderr is therefore consistent with the indexed backend genuinely running AND with this unwarned fallback.

So the one observable signal is not merely missing from `--json` -- it is INCONSISTENT ABOUT WHEN IT FIRES. That is worse than absent, because a partial signal invites exactly the inference that it is total, which is the inference opum-cli-e2e's row was making.

REQUIREMENT THIS ADDS: the `backend` field must be emitted on EVERY path, this one included. A field that reports the backend on two of three fallback routes reproduces the defect at higher resolution.

DELIBERATELY NOT RULED IN, and left as this repository's own call: whether the unwarned path should also warn. "Warn on every fallback" and "report the backend on every response" are different fixes; only the second is in scope here. Do not let the first expand into it silently. My own lean is that it should warn -- a silent fallback is the shape that hid LCLI-497 -- but that belongs in its own record, next to LCLI-498, rather than inside this one.

HOW IT WAS FOUND, because the method transfers: opum-cli-e2e wrote an assertion, opum-agent asked what it could actually prove, and it went back to lore's source rather than defending the row. Its check is now explicitly asymmetric -- presence of the advisory fails the row, absence is no longer read as success. That asymmetry stays correct even after this task lands.
references: LCLI-497 (the defect this absence let hide)
LCLI-498 (the fallback warning names no cause)
finalSummary:
Delivered in PR #78, CI run 34917232562 on head 72fb203c -- 10 checks SUCCESS, 2 SKIPPED (the promotion gates), none failed. That run validates the implementation; the closing commit adds tracker records only.

`lore graph`, `query`, `context`, `path` and `impact` now carry `data.backend` -- "indexed" or "reference" -- naming the retrieval backend that actually served the request.

AC1 -- the --json envelope of all five commands names the backend. Verified command by command in a test that drives each one through both an indexed and a reference loader and asserts the reported value matches. Measured against this repository: `lore graph --json`, `lore query lore --json` and `lore impact ... --json` all report "indexed".

AC2 -- present on every successful response, not only on a fallback. Asserted directly on a successful indexed run, together with the absence of any fallback advisory, so the test fails if the stamp is ever made conditional on degradation. Mutation-tested: making the stamp conditional on `backend === "reference"` -- a partial signal, which is precisely the defect this replaces -- fails 2 tests.

What makes the field total is STRUCTURAL rather than enumerated, and that is worth recording because it is the difference between a guarantee and a list. There is exactly one function producing a reference graph, and `backend` is a REQUIRED field on `RetrievalGraph`; a route cannot return one unstamped. The routes differ only in whether they ALSO warn -- and one of them, the path taken when no indexed generation exists, warns nothing at all. The test asserts the three routes drivable from the public options and states why the fourth is the identical call rather than pretending to cover it.

AC3 -- a test asserts the field for both an indexed and a reference-backed run of the same command. Five commands x two backends, in one case.

AC4 -- opum-cli-e2e has the field name and shape: `data.backend`, values "indexed" and "reference", on graph, query, context, path and impact. Sent with the PR link so their absence-assertion row can flip to a presence assertion.

A CONSEQUENCE THAT CHANGED MORE THAN THE FIELD DID. The two backends are required to produce the same answer and are now required to disagree about exactly one field, so every backend-parity comparison in this repository had to change: lore's indexed/reference conformance suite and the ladybug benchmark's parity gate both strip that one field, compare everything else byte-for-byte, and assert the stamp separately. Both are STRONGER for it -- they now check that each backend names itself, which byte equality never could.

The benchmark normalizes both parity quantities in ONE place, because `emittedBytes` is asserted equal across backends exactly like the digest and "indexed" and "reference" are different lengths. Normalizing the digest alone trades a digest mismatch for a byte-count mismatch and looks like a different defect -- which is what it did, for one iteration, before the normalization moved.

One synthetic fixture in the concurrency suite was given a real `--json` envelope in place of a placeholder object, because the parity assertion now reads `data.backend` and a fixture that does not look like the thing it stands for is how a check quietly stops covering the case it names.

DELIBERATELY NOT INCLUDED, per the ruling that scoped this task: making the unwarned fallback route warn. "Warn on every fallback" and "report the backend on every response" are different fixes; only the second was ruled in, and the first belongs next to LCLI-498, which is about that advisory naming no cause.

Validation: bun test 3030 pass / 1 skip / 0 fail; typecheck clean; lint clean; lore check 78 files, 0 errors, 0 warnings.
